name: Gershon
overview: Gershon was a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as a son of Levi. He is noted among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, and his descendants became known as the Gershonites, a significant Levitical family group.
namesAndTitles: The name Gershon means "temporary resident there," reflecting perhaps a transient status. A related form, Gershom, shares the same meaning, both names appearing in Scripture without indication of divine origin.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Gershon as a son of Levi. Inferred relationships associate him as an ancestor or father to several figures including Libni, Shimei, Jahath, and the ancestors Lael and Joel, indicating a lineage within the Levite family.
scriptureSignificance: Gershon's importance lies in his role as a progenitor of the Gershonite clan within the tribe of Levi. This clan held a distinct identity among the Levites, who were set apart for service to God. His inclusion in the list of those who went to Egypt highlights his place in the unfolding history of Israel's formation as a nation.
